note: Stated-assumption scenario shocks, in percent, per position. Judgements, not estimates: edit here; the dashboard, the published page and the PDF all read this file. The Korea line's shocks were set for ^KS11 and carried over unchanged when the book swapped it for EWY on 14 Oct 2026; EWY is in dollars, so a won move now lands inside the shock.

scenarios.name: Grid Bottleneck
scenarios.premise: Interconnection queues and transformer lead times, not chips, become the binding constraint on new capacity. Announced data-centre build slips.
scenarios.note: The thesis trade working: the bottleneck is physical, and the book is long the bottleneck.
rationale: URA, NLR, LB, PETR4.SA, 2222.SR: owners of power and land capture scarcity rent.
NBIS, CRWV: the neoclouds are the losers; they have signed for capacity they cannot energise, and their capex is already committed.
Compute lines: demand is deferred, not destroyed.
GLD, JPM, AVDV: Ballast roughly holds. RARA11.SA: rare earths bid on grid hardware demand.
ETN, HUBB: grid equipment is the scarce input, so its makers take the rent. ASML: tool orders defer with the compute build. IEUR: Europe is a bystander.

scenarios.name: CapEx Retrenchment
scenarios.premise: Hyperscalers cut AI capital spending guidance. The supercycle is re-rated as a cycle.
scenarios.note: The book's central risk. Note ballast is only {ballast:.0f}% — it cushions, it does not rescue.
rationale: Compute and neocloud lines take the hit first.
URA, NLR, LB, PETR4.SA, 2222.SR: fuel demand is a derivative of the buildout, so it goes too, just less, because reactors serve grids rather than data centres alone.
GLD, AVDV, JPM: this is the scenario Ballast exists for.
RARA11.SA: falls with the technology-materials cycle, so it does not cushion here.
ETN, HUBB: data-centre electrical orders fall, utility orders hold up better. ASML: tool orders are cut with foundry capex. IEUR: falls with global equity, less than US tech.

scenarios.name: Geopolitical Shock
scenarios.premise: A Taiwan Strait escalation. Advanced foundry output is interrupted and export controls tighten on strategic materials.
scenarios.note: Concentrated single-point risk: TSM, 2357.TW and EWY are one bet, not three.
rationale: TSM, 2357.TW, EWY: not a drawdown, an impairment. Three positions share one failure.
PLTR: defence-adjacent software is the one compute line that can rise.
Energy bids on supply fear; RARA11.SA bids hard on export controls.
ASML: export controls tighten and its largest customer's fabs stop. ETN, HUBB: industrial sell-off, orders intact. IEUR: risk-off and an ASML-heavy top holding.
